seeds.text: You don't find the path. You become it. There's no separate road — only the one your living shapes.
You are the world, and the world is you. The line between inner and outer is psychological, not real.
The wound is where the light enters. The places that broke open are the same places that became permeable to grace.
The softest things overcome the hardest. Yielding isn't weakness — it's a different kind of force.
Every ending is the shape of the next beginning. Same door, different side.

slides.composition: A shimmering, unfurled scroll of liquid chrome metal, subtly reflecting a starfield, filling the frame with ethereal glow.

slides.text: The path isn't ahead. It’s beneath your feet, forming with every single step.
slides.composition: An overhead view of a single chrome foot stepping onto shifting, pearlescent ground, radiating soft light outwards.

slides.text: Every true ending is not a wall, but a threshold. Same door, just a new world.
slides.composition: A monumental, ornate chrome archway, slightly glitching, frames a vast, painterly amber-violet cosmic landscape beyond.

slides.text: And the places that broke open? Those are your apertures. Where the deep light gets in.
slides.composition: A fractured, luminous crystal shard, emitting a prismatic rainbow burst, cradled gently by two cel-shaded anime hands.

slides.text: True strength isn't pushing. It’s the quiet art of letting life shape you.
slides.composition: A chrome liquid-metal figure, full-body in a soft, yielding pose, dissolving slightly into a deep navy dreamcore gradient.

slides.text: You're not finding a way. You're becoming the way. Your own unique, unrepeatable path.
slides.composition: A close-up of a human eye, iris reflecting a swirling nebula, with subtle VHS lines and a tiny 4-point sparkle.

slides.text: There's no wrong way to walk home.
slides.composition: A distant silhouette of a lone figure on a winding, chrome path, against a vast, soft pastel sky with glowing clouds.

caption:
For anyone feeling lost on the path, or wondering where the map is. What if the map is you, unfolding?
